_doc: Every closed vocabulary of the TKG English Learner's Dictionary, with a one-line description of each value. tools/validate.py enforces these; tools/build_site.py renders the labels and codes. A classifying field may hold only a value listed here. A new value is added only by a logged decision (wiki/decisions/) in the same pull request as the first entry that needs it. Keys are the exact strings stored in entries; 'code' is the short form shown beside the spelled-out label on the site.

n.label: noun
n.description: a word for a person, thing, place, quality, or idea

v.label: verb
v.description: a word for an action, event, or state

adj.label: adjective
adj.description: a word that describes a noun

adv.label: adverb
adv.description: a word that describes a verb, an adjective, another adverb, or a whole sentence

prep.label: preposition
prep.description: a word placed before a noun phrase to show a relation such as place, time, or direction

conj.label: conjunction
conj.description: a word that joins words, phrases, or clauses

pron.label: pronoun
pron.description: a word used in place of a noun phrase

det.label: determiner
det.description: a word placed before a noun to show which one or how many

num.label: number
num.description: a cardinal or ordinal number word

modal.label: modal verb
modal.description: a verb such as can or must used before another verb to express possibility, permission, or necessity

aux.label: auxiliary verb
aux.description: a helping verb such as be, have, or do used to form tenses, questions, and negatives

interj.label: interjection
interj.description: a word or sound used on its own to express a feeling or reaction

phrv.label: phrasal verb
phrv.description: a verb plus an adverb or preposition with a meaning of its own

phr.label: phrase
phr.description: a fixed expression with no single part of speech

prefix.label: prefix
prefix.description: a group of letters added to the beginning of a word to change its meaning

suffix.label: suffix
suffix.description: a group of letters added to the end of a word to change its meaning or part of speech

comb.label: combining form
comb.description: a word part used to form compounds, such as -phobia or eco-

abbr.label: abbreviation
abbr.description: a short form of a word or phrase, including initialisms and acronyms

countable.description: has a plural and can follow a or an: a book, two books

uncountable.description: has no plural and does not follow a or an: some water, a lot of information

countable or uncountable.description: used both ways, often with a difference of meaning: a coffee, some coffee

singular only.description: used only in the singular, usually with the or a possessive: the future, the outdoors, my whereabouts

plural only.description: used only in the plural and takes a plural verb: scissors, clothes

transitive.description: takes a direct object: She closed the door.

intransitive.description: takes no direct object: The door closed.

transitive or intransitive.description: used with or without a direct object in this sense

linking.description: joins the subject to a word that describes it: She seems tired.

verb + object.description: the verb is followed by a direct object

verb + two objects.description: the verb is followed by an indirect object and a direct object

verb + to-infinitive.description: the verb is followed by to and the base form of another verb

verb + object + to-infinitive.description: an object comes between the verb and to plus a base form

verb + bare infinitive.description: the verb is followed by a base form without to

verb + object + bare infinitive.description: an object comes between the verb and a base form without to

verb + -ing form.description: the verb is followed by the -ing form of another verb

verb + object + -ing form.description: an object comes between the verb and an -ing form

verb + that-clause.description: the verb is followed by a clause that can begin with that
verb + that-clause.example: She said that she was tired.

verb + object + that-clause.description: an object comes between the verb and a that-clause
verb + object + that-clause.example: He told me that it was late.

verb + wh-clause.description: the verb is followed by a clause beginning with a question word or whether

verb + object + wh-clause.description: an object comes between the verb and a clause beginning with a question word

verb + wh-word + to-infinitive.description: the verb is followed by a question word and to plus a base form

verb + adjective.description: the verb is followed by an adjective that describes the subject

verb + noun complement.description: the verb is followed by a noun phrase that describes the subject

verb + object + adjective.description: the verb is followed by an object and an adjective that describes it

verb + object + noun complement.description: the verb is followed by an object and a noun phrase that describes it

verb + object + as + noun or adjective.description: the verb is followed by an object, as, and a description of the object
verb + object + as + noun or adjective.example: We regard her as a friend.

verb + preposition + object.description: the verb needs a particular preposition before its object

verb + object + preposition + object.description: the verb takes an object and then a preposition with a second object
verb + object + preposition + object.example: She thanked him for the gift.

verb + adverb or preposition.description: the verb is used with an adverb or preposition particle and no object

verb + object + adverb.description: a separable phrasal verb with the object between the verb and the particle

verb + adverb + object.description: a phrasal verb with the object after the particle

verb + for + object + to-infinitive.description: the verb is followed by for, an object, and to plus a base form
verb + for + object + to-infinitive.example: We waited for the rain to stop.

verb + direct speech.description: the verb introduces or follows the exact words someone says

verb + object + past participle.description: the verb is followed by an object and a past participle

usually passive.description: in this sense the verb is used mostly in the passive
usually passive.example: The bridge was built in a year.

not used in the passive.description: in this sense the verb has no passive form
not used in the passive.example: This bag holds a lot. (not *A lot is held by this bag.)

not used in continuous tenses.description: in this sense the verb is not used in the -ing progressive forms
not used in continuous tenses.example: I know the answer. (not *I am knowing the answer.)

attributive only.description: used only before a noun: a mere child, not *the child is mere

predicative only.description: used only after a linking verb: the baby is asleep, not *an asleep baby

after the noun.description: placed after the noun it describes: the president elect, the people present

not gradable.description: has no comparative or superlative and is not used with very: dead, unique, daily

comparative with more.description: the comparative and superlative are formed with more and most, not -er and -est

usually plural.description: the noun is countable but normally used in the plural: circumstances, surroundings

usually singular.description: the noun is countable but normally used in the singular, often with a or the: a knack, the gist

singular or plural verb.description: a singular noun for a group that can take a singular or a plural verb: the team is or the team are

often before another noun.description: the noun is often used like an adjective before another noun: a business meeting

sentence adverb.description: the adverb comments on or connects a whole sentence: However, we stayed.

adjective + noun.description: adjectives that typically describe the noun: a heavy rain, a busy schedule

verb + noun.description: verbs that typically take the noun as their object: make a decision, catch a bus

noun + verb.description: verbs that the noun typically does: prices rise, a bomb goes off

noun + noun.description: compounds and noun modifiers: bank account, traffic jam

adverb + adjective.description: adverbs that typically strengthen or qualify the adjective: deeply grateful, fully aware

verb + adverb.description: adverbs that typically go with the verb: apologize profusely, listen carefully

adverb + verb.description: adverbs that typically come before the verb: strongly recommend, firmly believe

noun + preposition.description: prepositions that follow the noun: an interest in, a reason for

verb + preposition.description: prepositions that follow the verb: depend on, apply for

adjective + preposition.description: prepositions that follow the adjective: afraid of, keen on

preposition + noun.description: prepositions that go before the noun: at risk, in danger, on purpose

phrase.description: a fixed phrase built around the headword that is not an idiom: from time to time, sooner or later

synonym.description: a word with nearly the same meaning in this sense; listed under the sense, symmetric

antonym.description: a word with the opposite meaning in this sense; listed under the sense, symmetric

compare.description: a word learners confuse with this one or should see beside it; listed under the sense, symmetric

see also.description: a related entry worth reading; listed at entry level, not symmetric

word family.description: a word derived from or related in form to this one; listed at entry level, symmetric

formal.description: used in serious, official, or academic speech and writing; would sound stiff in casual talk

informal.description: used in casual speech and writing among friends and family; avoided in formal writing

very informal.description: used only in relaxed speech and casual messages; out of place in most writing

slang.description: very informal language used by a particular group, often new and often short-lived

humorous.description: used to be funny or playful

literary.description: found mainly in poetry, novels, and elevated writing, not in ordinary speech

technical.description: used mainly by specialists in the field named by the domain label

vulgar.description: a rude word for sex, the body, or body functions that many people find offensive

offensive.description: a word that insults or is likely to hurt a person or group; use with great care or not at all

polite.description: a word chosen to be respectful or to avoid a more direct word

childish.description: used by or to young children: tummy, doggie

region._doc: The variety of English in which the word or sense is mainly used. The set is open-ended by design so that World Englishes can be added by a logged decision; 'online' marks forms that belong to no region.

American.description: mainly used in the United States

British.description: mainly used in the United Kingdom

Caribbean.description: mainly used in the English-speaking Caribbean

online.description: used mainly in online writing and not tied to any region

domain._doc: The field of knowledge or activity a word or sense belongs to. Used only when the word is tied to the field, not for every word that can appear in it.

biology.description: living things and how they work

engineering.description: designing and building machines and structures

environment.description: the natural environment, pollution, and climate

geography.description: the earth's surface, maps, and places

geology.description: rocks and the structure of the earth

government.description: the state, public administration, and public services

grammar.description: the structure of language and terms for talking about it

human body.description: parts of the body and how it works

philosophy.description: ideas about knowledge, existence, and right and wrong

science.description: science in general, when no narrower field fits

sex.description: sex and sexuality, in neutral or clinical use

weather.description: weather and climate as experienced day to day

old-fashioned.description: still used and understood, but sounds like the language of an older generation

dated.description: no longer in ordinary use, though older people may use it and most people understand it

old use.description: no longer used at all except in old texts or deliberate imitation of them

historical.description: refers to something that belonged to the past and no longer exists; the word itself is current

new.description: came into use recently and may not last

approving.description: shows that the speaker admires or likes what is described

disapproving.description: shows that the speaker dislikes or criticizes what is described

ironic.description: used to mean the opposite of what it seems to say, often to be funny or critical

euphemistic.description: a gentler or less direct word for something unpleasant or embarrassing

affectionate.description: shows warmth or fondness toward the person or thing described

dismissive.description: treats the person or thing described as unimportant or not worth respect

semantic.description: how this word's senses split or merge in ways other languages commonly divide differently

grammar.description: a grammatical trap for learners from other languages: countability, argument structure, tense, preposition choice

culture.description: cultural or encyclopedic background a reader outside the English-speaking world needs

false_friends.description: a warning where an internationalism or look-alike in other languages differs in meaning

pronunciation.description: a sound, stress, or spelling-to-sound trap for learners in general

spelling.description: a different spelling of the same word: colour for color

form.description: a different form of the same word with the same meaning: amongst for among, gotten for got

plural.description: the plural form of a noun; null when the noun has no plural

third_person_singular.description: the present-tense form used with he, she, and it

past_participle.description: the form used after have and in the passive

comparative.description: the -er form; null when the comparative is made with more or the word is not gradable

superlative.description: the -est form; null when the superlative is made with most or the word is not gradable

rules.description: generated by the regular rules in tools/inflect.py

none.description: the part of speech does not inflect

verified.description: checked by the agreement rule in wiki/decisions/pronunciation-pipeline.md, or generated by a rule or the exceptions table

disputed.description: the checks disagreed; the entry carries a flag and the question is in reviews/needs_curator.txt

unverified.description: no check has been made yet, or the check could not be completed

draft.description: written but not yet through the full pipeline; never published

reviewed.description: schema-valid, pronunciation and inflections verified or flagged, both reviewers run, every blocking issue adjudicated; published

pronunciation-disputed.description: the pronunciation panel disagreed and the open data did not settle it

pronunciation-unverified.description: the pronunciation check could not be run

inflection-disputed.description: the inflection rules and the reviewers disagreed

inflection-unverified.description: the inflection rules could not decide a form

label-disputed.description: the reviewers disagreed about a usage label and no open data bears on it

grammar-disputed.description: the reviewers disagreed about a grammar code or pattern

fact-disputed.description: the reviewers disagreed about a factual claim in a note

needs-curator.description: a question about this entry is waiting in reviews/needs_curator.txt

declined-in-part.description: the drafting model declined to write one or more fields; the entry says which

ok.description: the reviewer found nothing wrong with the field

issue.description: the reviewer found a problem; the exact claim is quoted, with a severity, a family, and a one-line reason

blocking.description: the entry must not be published until this is fixed or rejected with a reason

minor.description: worth fixing, but the entry can be published as it stands

apply.description: the session agreed with the reviewer and changed the entry

reject.description: the session disagreed with the reviewer and left the entry as it was; the reason is logged

escalate.description: the session could not decide; the question went to reviews/needs_curator.txt and the entry carries a flag

definition-meaning.description: the definition is wrong, misleading, or misses the sense

definition-style.description: the definition is circular, padded, not phrasal, or too hard for the reader

definition-vocabulary.description: the definition uses a word outside the defining vocabulary that has no entry

explanation.description: the plain-prose explanation is wrong or unhelpful

example-unnatural.description: an example is unidiomatic, awkward, or unlike real use

example-grammar.description: an example is ungrammatical or does not show the sense or pattern claimed

example-policy.description: an example breaks the example rules: real-world facts, brand names, culturally loaded names or settings

grammar-code.description: a countability, transitivity, pattern, or grammar code is wrong or missing

label.description: a register, region, domain, currency, or attitude label is wrong or missing

collocation.description: a collocation is wrong, unnatural, or wrongly typed

cross-reference.description: a synonym, antonym, compare, see-also, or word-family reference is wrong

learner-error.description: a learner-error item is wrong or its correction is wrong

synonym-discrimination.description: the synonym-discrimination note is wrong or misleading

usage-note.description: a claim in the usage note is wrong

etymology.description: the etymology is wrong, unverified, or not relevant to current use

sense-structure.description: a sense is missing, over-split, wrongly ordered, or its signpost or the core idea misleads

phrase.description: an idiom or fixed-phrase sub-entry is wrong or misplaced

adaptation.description: an adaptation note is wrong, not language-neutral, or over the word cap

spelling-or-format.description: a spelling mistake, an abbreviation, or a formatting slip in a prose field

other.description: an issue that fits no family above; the reason says what it is

pending.description: in the queue, not yet claimed by any run

claimed.description: listed in a claim file by a run that has not yet merged its entry

declined.description: the drafting model declined to write the entry; the reason is in the queue note

deferred.description: set aside by a logged decision; the note says why and until when

duplicate.description: the same lexical item is already in the queue or the dictionary under another row

defining.description: a member of the defining vocabulary

band.description: added by the frequency-band estimation of wiki/decisions/defining-vocabulary.md

closure.description: used in a definition, example, or note without having an entry (found by tools/lint_vocab.py)

family.description: named in a word-family box without having an entry

crossref.description: named as a synonym, antonym, compare, or see-also target without having an entry

owner.description: requested by the owner through inbox/

world.description: World Englishes and online English, added in the later phase

1.label: very common
1.description: the defining vocabulary and the words every learner meets first

2.label: common
2.description: words most intermediate learners know or need soon

3.label: fairly common
3.description: words an upper-intermediate learner meets in ordinary reading

4.label: less common
4.description: words an advanced learner meets in wide reading

draft.description: written but not checked by a speaker of the language
